tasks.title: Prove one product feat on two stacks
tasks.goal: Implement one unchanged feat intent in Rust and TypeScript fixture consumers with independent evidence.
steps: Create one exact captured feat definition and two small existing-code fixture consumers using supported Rust and TypeScript stack contracts.
Apply the same origin through M-03 existing-file production and verify current source with each stack's declared checks.
Retain independent requests/output/evidence/closure per consumer; compare origin captures to prove no stack-specific feat copy.
positive_cases: Both stacks satisfy the same unchanged feat intent with actual existing-file changes.
Each consumer has its own accepted boundary and source-test identity.
negative_cases: Disjoint output-only demo or predecessor tests from old source fail the gate.
Changing the origin definition for one stack violates reuse.
acceptance: Two distinct consumer evidence chains point to one origin capture.
Actual stack commands are recorded and checked; source tests are not inferred from a generic green handler.
tasks.safe_stop: First feat × two stacks is proven; second feat remains mandatory.
tasks.commit_subject: test(examples): prove one feat across two existing-code stacks
notes: Stack fixture files/check commands are TO CREATE from supported stack contracts; record exact commands before execution. Root supplies prepared runtimes; no guessed npm scripts.
Registration perimeter includes existing crate manifests and module owners only for required exports/dependencies; do not change unrelated declarations.

tasks.title: Prove a second feat and explicit origin drift handling
tasks.goal: Complete the two-by-two reuse matrix and verify consumer rebase behavior.
steps: Add a substantively different second feat using the same two stack fixtures and full current-source evidence route.
Change an origin capture at the same version and inspect each consumer's drift independently; require explicit rebase before new applicability.
Record the complete four-cell reuse matrix, retained original captures and independent acceptance; do not reuse one consumer's verdict for another.
positive_cases: Two unchanged feat origins each work in both stacks.
Explicit rebase binds the selected new capture without rewriting historical evidence.
negative_cases: Same-version source drift cannot silently relabel old closure.
One failed/missing matrix cell keeps the reuse deliverable incomplete.
acceptance: Four actual runs have exact source/output/test and origin references.
Historical acceptance remains inspectable and stale applicability is explicit.
tasks.safe_stop: Two-by-two proof and drift/rebase evidence are ready for review.
tasks.commit_subject: test(examples): complete feat reuse and origin drift matrix
notes: Registration perimeter includes existing crate manifests and module owners only for required exports/dependencies; do not change unrelated declarations.
